lines.text: This pink rock from the Sahara isn't from Earth. It's a piece of Mars.
It was found in Mali in 2022. Scientists call it Teghaza 001.
To date it, they looked inside tiny zircon crystals. Uranium in them slowly turns into lead, like a built-in clock.
That clock says the rock formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. NASA says it's one of the three oldest Mars meteorites found on Earth.
Its minerals match what NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter sees in the cratered southern highlands. The team found 13 possible places it came from.
And it hides a clue about water. The lead scientist says Mars' surface had water more than 4.1 billion years ago.
The study, led by NASA's JPL, is published in Science. A desert rock, carrying a message from early Mars.
